skill.name: making-commits
skill.description: Guidance for creating small, focused Git commits and running quality checks before committing.
skill.summary: Helps agents keep Git commit history clear and maintainable.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: No static findings were reported for this prompt-only skill. Manual review found no prompt injection, credential handling, executable code, network access, or filesystem operations in SKILL.md.

content.value_statement: Large changes often produce messy commit history that slows review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to make small commits with quality checks.
actual_capabilities: Encourages small commits that address one concern or feature.
Guides agents to split large changes into logical commit groups.
Reminds agents to run linting and formatting before committing.
Supports cleaner review history for larger coding tasks.
Provides lightweight commit hygiene guidance without running tools.
limitations: Does not create commits or execute Git commands by itself.
Does not define a commit message format or naming convention.
Does not inspect repository state, staged files, or branch history.
Does not run linters, formatters, tests, or security checks.

use_cases.title: Prepare Reviewable Feature Work
use_cases.description: Split a larger feature into focused commits before opening a pull request.

use_cases.title: Clean Up Agent-Generated Changes
use_cases.description: Guide an AI coding agent to group generated edits into logical commit steps.

use_cases.title: Maintain Project Commit Hygiene
use_cases.description: Remind contributors to run formatting and linting before recording project changes.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Small Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current changes and suggest a small, focused commit plan. Keep each commit limited to one concern.

prompt_templates.title: Group Related Changes
prompt_templates.prompt: Group these edits into logical commits for review. Identify any change that should be separated before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Check Commit Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Before I commit, verify that the change groups are focused and list the linting or formatting checks I should run.

prompt_templates.title: Structure a Large Task History
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a commit sequence for this larger task. Separate setup, implementation, tests, and cleanup into reviewable steps.

output_examples.input: I changed the API client, updated tests, and reformatted unrelated files.
output_examples.output: Suggested split: one commit for API client behavior, one commit for related tests, and one separate formatting commit if needed.

output_examples.input: I finished a large feature and want a clean pull request history.
output: Start with dependency or setup changes.
Commit the core feature implementation separately.
Add tests in a focused follow-up commit.
Run linting and formatting before the final commit.

best_practices: Keep each commit focused on one concern or feature.
Split large changes into logical review steps.
Run linting and formatting before creating commits.
anti_patterns: Combining unrelated fixes, features, and formatting in one commit.
Committing large tasks without a clear review sequence.
Skipping formatting or linting before recording changes.

faq.question: Does this skill run Git commands?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance only and does not execute commands.

faq.question: Can it write commit messages?
faq.answer: It can help plan commits, but the source does not define a message format.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What problem does it solve?
faq.answer: It helps keep commit history focused, readable, and easier to review.

faq.question: Should I still run tests?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill mentions linting and formatting, but it does not replace tests.

faq.question: Is this a security-sensitive skill?
faq.answer: No evidence found. It is a prompt-only skill with no executable code or external access.
